Hi Emily —

Thanks again for agreeing to let Redwood highlight Axon Medical in a short customer spotlight. Attached is the draft (axon_case_draft_v2.docx) and a small metrics file with the throughput/latency numbers we cited. We want to make sure all technical facts and the pull-quote representing your product team are accurate before we publish.

Could you please:
- Review the draft and mark any factual corrections inline (esp. the section under "Deployment & Performance").
- Confirm the quote attributed to Alex Martin (VP Eng) — we can revise the phrasing if it needs to be more conservative.
- Let us know if legal needs to review for brand or regulatory language.

If it's easier, here's a Google Doc link with suggested edits enabled: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aXonCaseDraftV3

Target timeline: if we can get approval or redlines by end of week (Fri 12/3) we can schedule a short promo drop the following week.

Appreciate it —
Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the draft and the clear notes. Quick inline notes below (copied from the Google Doc). High level: happy to be featured but we do need a couple corrections and a more measured quote.

Inline redlines (high level):
- Deployment & Performance: the draft lists "20-30% latency reduction" — our benchmarking showed ~14% median latency reduction at 95th percentile when switching to Redwood's batching config. Please change the statistic to "~14% median latency reduction at 95th percentile" or remove the percentile and say "~14% median latency reduction".
- Cost savings: we prefer "unit cost improved by ~22% on production workloads" rather than an absolute $ figure.
- Customer quote: Alex prefers this variant: "Redwood lets our team ship low-latency features without us building complex serving infrastructure — the performance has been reliably better in production." (please attribute to Alex Martin, VP of Engineering).
- Regulatory blurb: please avoid implying we store PHI; we only process de-identified telemetry for model tuning.

Legal has asked to see the final copy before publish; I've cc'd them. Product Ops also wants to check the timeline. We can do final signoff by our CCO once legal confirms the non-PHI wording.

On timing: we can aim for next Tue 12/7 for final approval if you incorporate these edits and circulate an updated draft today or tomorrow.

Emily Chen
Head of Product | Axon Medical
emily.chen@axonmedical.com
+1 212-555-9876

Emily / Karthik — looping in marketing/legal notes from our side. Thanks for the careful review, Emily. I made the suggested changes in the Google Doc and replaced the raw $ number with "~22% improvement in unit cost" per your ask.

A few small edits we made:
- Adjusted the performance stat to say "~14% median latency reduction at 95th percentile" and added a short parenthetical: "(Axon internal benchmark, November 2026)".
- Reworded the regulatory sentence to: "Axon Medical only provides de-identified telemetry used for aggregate model tuning; no PHI is included in the data shared with Redwood."
- Quote: updated to the Alex Martin variant and shortened slightly to fit the article tone.

Emily, can you please confirm the parenthetical benchmark phrasing is acceptable to your team and legal? If legal wants the benchmark language removed entirely we can say "internal benchmarks" without numbers.

I also attached the updated draft (axon_case_draft_v3.docx) to the Google Doc. If we get a thumbs up by EOD tomorrow we can lock and schedule publish activities.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

If you can send the final with our byline and updated paragraph order, I will route to CCO for final sign-off. Targeting Tue 12/7 for the publish window works for us.
